title: How better climate diplomacy can save Europe’s green ambitions – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: A policy alert arguing that EU industrial decarbonisation front-runners in steel and chemicals are being squeezed by war-driven energy prices, Chinese competition and rising emissions-trading costs while the rest of the world moves too slowly, and that Brussels' climate diplomacy is misdirected at general mitigation and finance instead of industrial-transformation partnerships. It notes the Commission proposed weakening EU emissions trading on 17 July 2026 while strengthening green-transition support.

themes.theme: Cost squeeze on EU heavy industry

insights.claim: EU steel and chemicals producers face a compounding cost squeeze: energy prices pushed up by Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine and the US-Israel-Iran conflict, fierce Chinese competition in chemicals, fertilisers and steel, and rising emissions-trading costs.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Three simultaneous margin headwinds on EU basic-materials names; watch carbon cost pass-through and import share in chemicals and fertilisers.
insights.quote: Now Russia’s full-scale war in Ukraine and the US-Israel-Iran conflict are pushing up energy prices; there is fierce competition from China and others for products such as chemicals, fertilisers and steel.

insights.claim: EU first-mover advantage in low-carbon industrial products is real but has come with transition costs concentrated in steel and chemicals, and the rest of the world is not decarbonising fast enough to close the cost gap for European front-runners.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Green-premium business models in EU materials depend on foreign policy closing the cost differential, not on technology alone.
insights.quote: Other parts of the world are not moving fast enough to reduce cost differences for European front-runner companies

insights.claim: The 2025 IEA Breakthrough Agenda report finds global low-carbon industrial transitions are happening too slowly to achieve the targets of the Paris Agreement.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Authoritative confirmation that industrial-decarbonisation demand will lag policy targets — discount near-term green-materials volume forecasts.
insights.locator: the 2025 IEA Breakthrough Agenda report shows

insights.claim: On 17 July 2026 the European Commission proposed weakening EU emissions trading to accommodate industry while simultaneously strengthening its support mechanism for green transitions.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Directly bearish for EUA carbon prices and bullish for subsidy-dependent decarbonisation capex; a concrete dated catalyst to trade around.
insights.quote: on July 17th the European Commission proposed weakening EU emission trading to accommodate industry while simultaneously strengthening its support mechanism for green transitions

insights.claim: The EU retains ambitious 2030 and 2040 climate targets and a 2050 climate-neutrality goal, but the policy instruments meant to deliver them are now being hotly contested.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Target-level rhetoric is a poor guide to instrument strength — price the instruments, not the targets.

insights.claim: EU climate diplomacy is under-prioritising partnerships for industrial decarbonisation and instead focuses on general mitigation and financing issues.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: The gap is where new EU money and partnership deals will land if the argument wins — watch the Global Europe instrument.
insights.locator: At the EU level, climate diplomacy is not sufficiently prioritising

insights.claim: The EU Task Force for International Carbon Pricing and Markets Diplomacy launched in 2024 did not address infrastructure development, access to finance, intellectual property rights or personnel skills — the actual enablers of industrial decarbonisation abroad.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
entities: EU Task Force for International Carbon Pricing and Markets Diplomacy
insights.so_what: Identifies the specific unfunded workstreams likely to attract new EU instruments and vendor opportunity.
insights.locator: While the launch of the EU Task Force

insights.claim: The author urges ministers to write industrial transformation diplomacy into the strategic roadmap document and to push for adequate funding in the next 'Global Europe' development-policy instrument.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: A named budget line to monitor for the next EU external-spending cycle.
insights.locator: Ministers should include industrial transformation diplomacy

insights.claim: An informal meeting of EU environment and climate ministers on 23-24 July 2026 carried both decarbonisation-and-competitiveness and climate diplomacy on its agenda, which the author argues must be treated as a single integrated file.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Near-dated policy event whose framing determines whether competitiveness relief or diplomacy funding dominates.

insights.claim: China, Japan and South Korea are held up as models because they have the institutional capacity to make strategic choices about which technologies to support and a designed mix of instruments to promote them — capacity the EU lacks.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Signals EU drift toward explicit technology-picking industrial policy, which favours incumbents in designated strategic sectors.
insights.quote: which have the institutional capacity to make strategic choices about which technology to support
insights.locator: The EU should learn from the more active industrial policies

insights.claim: European coal-region transitions, notably in Poland, are presented as an exportable blueprint for building public acceptance of closing mines and winding down fossil-dependent manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Just-transition consultancy and reskilling programmes become an EU export product tied to partnership funding.
insights.locator: Europeans should also look at how European coal regions

insights.claim: The author argues no single member state — not even Germany — can build partnerships strong enough to meet the China challenge alone, requiring a 'Team Europe' approach plus more climate-diplomacy staffing in Brussels and EU delegations.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Bilateral German industrial diplomacy is being written off — expect EU-level consortium structures to become the contracting vehicle.
insights.quote: even big member states such as Germany cannot build strong enough partnerships alone
insights.locator: The EU must address the lack of coherence

insights.claim: EU environment ministers began a process to improve climate diplomacy after what many saw as disappointing, weak language on reducing overall emissions at COP30 in Belém in 2025, but that process has focused on formal negotiation prep rather than broader industrial partnerships.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Low bar going into COP31 — expect EU deliverables to be process rather than emissions commitments.

insights.claim: Brazil's 2025 initiative launched a process for accelerating low-carbon transformation of industry under the Paris Agreement, and Turkey intends to continue that work at COP31 in November 2026.
insights.speaker: Mats Engström
insights.so_what: Industrial decarbonisation is the live COP31 workstream — position around November 2026 Turkey summit deliverables.
